title: Forge 6: initialisation, BatchNorm and LayerNorm

wrong.he_std_missing_two.py: he_std is sqrt(1/fan_in): the factor 2 that pays for ReLU zeroing half the units is missing, so the signal halves per layer
wrong.init_not_seeded.py: init_weights ignores its seed, so runs are not reproducible
wrong.init_unknown_kind_silent.py: an unknown kind silently falls back to He instead of raising
wrong.bn_unbiased_forward.py: the batch is normalised with the unbiased variance (ddof=1) instead of the biased one
wrong.bn_running_var_biased.py: the running variance uses the biased batch variance (missing N/(N-1))
wrong.bn_momentum_swapped.py: the running average weights are swapped: momentum multiplies the OLD value
wrong.bn_eval_uses_batch_stats.py: evaluation mode still normalises with the current batch's statistics
wrong.bn_eval_updates_running.py: evaluation mode also updates the running statistics
wrong.bn_dx_ignores_batch_stats.py: backward treats mean and variance as constants: dx = dout*gamma*inv_std (a plausible shortcut that is wrong in training mode)
wrong.bn_eps_outside_sqrt.py: eps is added to the standard deviation instead of the variance
wrong.bn_dgamma_without_xhat.py: dgamma sums dout without multiplying by xhat
wrong.bn_single_example_allowed.py: training mode accepts a batch of one (variance 0, output is just beta) instead of raising
wrong.bn_no_train_flag.py: train() and eval() do not change the mode
wrong.ln_normalises_over_batch.py: LayerNorm reduces over axis 0 (the batch) instead of the last axis
wrong.ln_dgamma_not_summed.py: dgamma/dbeta are not summed over the leading axes, so they have the wrong shape for 3-D input
wrong.ln_no_eps.py: eps is dropped, so a constant row divides by zero
wrong.ln_dx_missing_mean_terms.py: backward keeps only dxhat*inv_std and drops the mean and variance terms
wrong.ln_accumulates.py: dgamma accumulates across calls instead of being set

hints: Initialisation is two one-liners plus a seeded rng.normal scaled by the std. The interesting part is *why*: Var(y) = fan_in * Var(w) * E[x^2].
BatchNorm forward in training: mean = x.mean(0), var = x.var(0) (numpy's default is the biased variance, which is what you want for normalising). Cache xhat and 1/sqrt(var+eps) for backward.
The running variance uses var * N/(N-1). The running update is running = (1-momentum)*running + momentum*batch_stat.
dx = inv_std / N * (N*dxhat - dxhat.sum(0) - xhat * (dxhat*xhat).sum(0)), with dxhat = dout * gamma. dgamma = (dout*xhat).sum(0), dbeta = dout.sum(0).
LayerNorm is the same formulas with axis=-1 and keepdims=True, and N replaced by the feature count D. If a gradient check fails, check the reduction axes first.
